subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose a plugin runtime caller for plugin-registered Gateway methods, and if so should it be raw dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: Current main intentionally limits Gateway requests to bundled or trusted official plugins, while this issue asks to extend the public SDK boundary to third-party inter-plugin communication.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only dispatch
options.body: Decline ordinary external plugin Gateway calls and require plugins to use existing HTTP route, typed runtime helper, or plugin-specific capability seams.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and accept a much larger security and compatibility surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current dispatch entitlement boundary and is the strongest history match for the Plugin SDK/Gateway authorization decision.
